Subject: Burn profile & warm-cache impact — renewal options

Hi Ari / Tara,

Thanks again for the time last week. We ran the usage cohort analysis you asked for and attached the Q3_burn_profile.csv plus a short bench on our warm-cache behavior (warm_cache_bench.pdf). High-level summary below: 

- Net token burn in Q3: 18.4M tokens (up 42% vs Q2) driven by a 3x increase in repeat chat sessions from the mobile client.
- Peak concurrency: 420 reqs/min, sustained at ~220 reqs/min outside spikes.
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile at 320ms on your current model mix (no quantization).
- Warm-cache (prefix/KV) effect: experiments show ~22% reduction in end-to-end per-token cost with negligible latency change when warm-cache retained across sessions for top 15% of users. See attached bench PDF.

Implications for renewal / term sizing: 
1) Short-term (6 months): commit to a 25% uplift in reserved capacity + burst credits. This covers projected Q4 growth while preserving cost parity vs on-demand.
2) Mid-term (12 months): shift to a stepped commit with auto-tranche at 50% utilization to avoid over-commit. We model two pricing scenarios in term_scenarios.xlsx (attached) — conservative vs aggressive.

ROI snapshot (conservative): estimated monthly net savings from warm-cache + reserved pricing = ~$8.5k, payback on engineering toggles ~2.5 months once warm-cache retention is enabled and client-side session affinity is configured.

Ask: can we get a decision preference (6m reserve vs 12m stepped) by Oct 13? If helpful, we can run a 48-hour load test with warm-cache enabled on a slice of traffic next week.

Thanks,
Olga

Subject: Internal: Quick ROI and tier suggestion for Brightleaf

Internal note — copying into thread when we send the recommendation. Key points: 

- Using the attached term_scenarios.xlsx I ran a blended unit-cost model. With warm-cache enabled for the high-frequency cohort (top 15%), effective per-1000-token cost drops ~18% after amortizing reserved capacity benefits.
- Recommendation A (low risk): 6-month reserved + 25k burst credits. Keeps Brightleaf flexible, covers 95th percentile spikes, and shows a ~9% TCO improvement year-on-year.
- Recommendation B (growth-minded): 12-month stepped commit: 30% baseline commit with two automatic tranches (at 50% and 80% utilization). This reduces effective unit cost by ~14% vs 6-month option and is preferable if they expect sustained >40% QoQ growth.
- Risk notes: if they enable aggressive prefetch/warm-cache and then roll it back, cost improvement reverses quickly — include a clause in the SOW about preferred client-side session affinity best practices.

Planned reply: propose both options, include explicit burst pricing table and offer the 48-hour test + request logs.

Ari / Tara —

Appreciate the quick questions. Short answers up front: 
1) Warm-cache reduction: the 22% figure is for generation tokens only (model decode). We see small extra impact (~3%) on embedding-heavy pipelines because fewer full-context recomputations are needed; I called out the decode benefit because it’s the primary spend bucket.
2) Burst credits: for the 6-month option we price bursts at 1.6x on-demand for tokens beyond committed corridor (we give a 10% free tier of burst within each invoice period). If you prefer a fixed top-up rate we can lock a lower burst multiplier for the 12m stepped commit.

Proposal (summarized):
- Option 1 — 6 months: 25% reserved uplift + 25k burst credits; on-bill pricing shows ~9% YoY TCO reduction.
- Option 2 — 12 months: stepped commit (30% baseline) with auto-tranching and lower burst multiplier; shows ~14% TCO reduction and preferred for sustained growth scenarios.

Next steps: 
- Confirm which option you want us to formalize by Oct 13.
- We’ll schedule the 48-hour warm-cache load test for Tue/Wed next week (need your ops contact for request-log access).
- If you want, we can include a line in the SOW for a warm-cache enablement playbook (one-time implementation fee).

If agreeable, I’ll drop a short one-pager and an updated pricing table into HubSpot and send a DocuSign-ready addendum.

Thanks — looking forward to your preferred path.
